user_query: I want to write a will.
variations: How do I make a will in Singapore?
Can I write my own will?
How much does a will cost?
I want to distribute my assets after I die
part_a_general_info: A will must be in writing, signed by you, and witnessed by two witnesses who are not beneficiaries of the will. These formalities are set out in the Wills Act 1838. You can write your own will (DIY), but this carries risks of ambiguity or invalid provisions. It is recommended to seek legal advice. CPF savings are NOT covered by your will. You must make a separate CPF nomination with the CPF Board. HDB flats held under joint tenancy pass automatically to the surviving owner and are not governed by the will. It is not mandatory to register your will, but you can deposit information about its location with the Wills Registry.
triage_questions: Q1: Do you have specific assets (property, bank accounts, investments) you wish to distribute?
Q2: Do you have dependents (spouse, children, elderly parents)?
Q3: Have you made a CPF nomination?
Q4: How is your property held (joint tenancy or tenancy-in-common)?
branching_logic: If Q3 = no CPF nomination → Advise to make one separately.
If Q4 = joint tenancy → Inform that property passes automatically to surviving owner.
routing: Route A (Standard will preparation): Pro Bono SG does not draft wills. Refer to private law firms via the Law Society directory. Inform about free will-writing events if available.
Route B (Low-income applicant): Refer to Legal Aid Bureau if applicant qualifies (means test). Some pro bono will-writing clinics may be available.
guardrail: Must NOT draft or prepare any will. This is expressly prohibited under s.33 of the Legal Profession Act.
